lines.en: You know...there’s really nothing about today that makes much sense when you look at how I’ve approached my relationship with Ami as a whole.

I mean, sure. We’ve gone on a number of trips together. And we’ve made more memories along the way than I ever would have assumed I’d make when I first opened my eyes and saw her standing there in the sunlight.
I had no idea who she was. And hearing that from me directly was probably startling despite how easily she played it off as some sort of memory lapse.
I wonder just how many times she’s had to do such a thing — or how many times she’s had to kick herself into a shape that believes all that really was just some sort of post-nap daze.
The point is, though...if today is meant to be a day of new beginnings, it should be a day where the me I left at home would be unable to predict the actions of the me that’s in the woods.
And since everything else has gone completely against my character so far, there’s only one person I can think of talking to right now if I want to keep that pattern up.
So I tap on her name in my phone and wait for her to answer.
: Hello?
: Hey. What’s up?
: Sir?!
: That’s right.
: I know it’s right! I just don’t know why it’s right. Mayhap you’ve called the wrong number?
: Or better yet! You’ve been stricken with a deadly ailment and are now saying goodbye to everyone you know in the order of least to most appreciated!
: Right again. And you just happen to be the last person on that list.
: Roll for deception.
: One million.
: All I heard was “one.” Which means you’ve critically failed as I already know you’ve yet to speak with the Kendo Princess.
: Tsuneyo’s with you?
: Aye. We’re at the arcade. Would you like me to pass on a greeting?
: No.
: Who is that?
: It is the Supreme Overlord. He’s dialed my number on accident. Would you like me to pass on a greeting?
: No.
: Do the two of you even like one another?
: Not really.
: She’s fine.
: Sir, apologies for repeating the transmission, but why are you calling me exactly? I was under the impression you were still under the effects of corrupted blood.
: Is that another video game reference?
: Only to the deadliest plague in MMO history! No one was safe, Sir! The entire world needed to be reset and repaired before it went away!
: Yeah well, that’s definitely a realistic way of fixing things. So hey, maybe I just need to wait for that to happen in order to feel normal again?
: Tuesday is just around the corner, Sir. Bug fixes should be rolling out.
: Then it seems I have something to look forward to.
: Sir-
: I just wanted to hear your voice.
: You...

: You what? Apologies again, Sir. I believe my delusions of grandeur may have finally begun rewriting reality in a way that causes me to overwrite actual dialogue with what you’d say as a character in a dating sim.
: I said I wanted to hear your voice.
: Gods help me. What if this is permanent?
: Your face has changed colors, Emerald Guardian. And I know you well enough to understand that you must either be aroused or embarrassed if this is the case. Which one is it?
: Both I think.
: I just figured talking to you might be a nice change of pace since this admittedly isn’t a thing I do all that often.
: I’ll say, Sir. It’s been so long that I was taken quite aback when I saw Arthas Menethil’s name pop up on my screen just now.
: I don’t know how to tell you this, but that is not my name and I’m not sure where you heard that.

: The name matters not, Sir. It’s just how you’re labeled in my phone. But what is all of this about a change of pace? Have things truly gotten so terrible that you’re looking to me of all people for help?
: I guess so. But today isn’t really that bad, all things considered. In fact, it’s actually been pretty good so far. Just...different.
: If you’re hanging out with Tsuneyo though, I can just call back some other time.
: She actually just left!
: Who left?
: I can hear her.
: Geh!
: Oh. It appears a telepathic communication is coming in.
: I must listen closely so the sounds are not muddled by various action games.
: Is everything-
: One moment...Sir! Channelling...my energy!
: Message received. Rail everyone.
: Wow, that worked too.
: What worked? What’s going on?
: Not much, Sir. Just, between this and the recent Dorm Wars, I’m beginning to think that some of my quirks aren’t actually fake after all.
: So we can keep talking?
: We can talk for as long as you like! I’m still just confused as to why!

: Like I said, I just wanted to try something different. And there’s no greater change of pace than going from talking to Ami then talking to the Emerald Molly of the MacCormack Jungle or whatever it was.

: That was so far off that I can’t help but feel somewhat offended, Sir. But still, is that alone enough to warrant seeking me out? I’ve proven on several occasions now that there’s nothing I can do to help you.
: Which depresses me greatly as I would very much LIKE to help you. I’m just not sure if a phone call alone will be enough to do that. But, then again, nor would meeting in person...so...
: I’m not asking you to specifically do something that will help, Molly. I’m just asking you to exist. And to continue existing for at least the duration of this call.
: I have no plans to stop existing, Sir. And I’m happy to hear your voice as well.
: I’ve actually been thinking about you a lot lately.
: In what way?
: Mostly just wondering when I’ll be able to see you again. The dorms have gotten rather lonely in the wake of your departure, Sir. The halls still call your name just as they did in days past.
: Again, hate to be the bearer of bad news, but that probably wasn’t the hall you heard calling my name.
: And I’m sure it’s not the hall I’ve been hearing call it recently either but rather someone else struggling with your absence, Sir.
: Well, it’s good to see that not much has changed on that end I guess.
: Good for you, perhaps. But all of us can’t stop wondering when we’ll be able to see you again. Your company may as well require a lottery ticket at this point in time, Sir.
: Then you can view this call as me trying to combat that to some extent.
: I know that things have to change. And I know that there are certain things I’m going to have to do if Ami is ever going to regain some normalcy in her life.
: But what about you, Sir?
: What do you mean?
: What about you regaining some sort of normalcy in your life? Because your prior proposal made it sound more like you’re just doing this for Arborea’s sake.
: Oh. Well, that’s because I am.
: Then that’s not good at all, Sir! And this is coming from someone who quite literally has devoted herself to a variety of fictional characters!
: Then you should understand better than most what it means to live for someone else and not yourself. Just, in my case, it’s a living human. And in yours, it’s probably a werewolf or something.
: I believe you may have me confused with Noriko, Sir. Which would actually explain this call quite well if you had not already addressed me by name.
: Is Noriko also into werewolves?
: The word “also” implies that I am into them as well, Sir.
: Are you not?
: No comment.
: Yeah, that’s what I thought.
: All yiff aside, Sir- there’s something I’m rather curious about.
: Probably not the best time to ask about whether or not I’m still up for sexual experimentation with you.
: Oh, don’t worry. I’ve done enough of that in recent days and don’t mind another period of waiting before something else enters my body.
: Wow. What the hell have you been getting up to while I’ve been away?
: Losing the last shred of my dignity, Sir.
: That is not what I had in mind, but I will make a mental note of this so I do not accidentally disgust you again.
: Regardless, the thing I’m curious about is exactly what you’re up to at the moment as you’ve alluded to the day being rather different and I’m not quite sure what that means.
: Have you and Arborea departed the inn on a fetch quest? Is your party larger than just the two of you? What’s going on precisely?
: I’m camping.
: Camping? Like...outside?
: Weird, right?
: But...outside is where the sun is, Sir. You don’t mean to tell me you’re willingly spending time under such an evil entity, do you?
: There are a few trees blocking it out, but yeah. This is where the sun is.
: Should I send help? I can have a gryphon headed your way in no time at all, Sir. Just do not be alarmed if that gryphon is disguised as a taxi.
: It’s fine, Molly. And yes, this is definitely something I’d never come up with on my own. But I needed to get Ami out of the house somehow and I figured she’d enjoy something like this.
: But then why are you talking to me? You should be with her if you’re really doing this to try and make her happy, Sir.
: I can’t. She’s been kidnapped.
: Just out of curiosity, what percentage of this conversation has been entirely fabricated so far?
: Because I’m starting to think it’s all of it and that you really did somehow roll a one million on that deception check earlier.
: Everything has been real, Molly.
: Ami’s with a friend of mine right now. And I’m fine with it because she’s another girl that’s my age and Ami really needs a mother figure right now.
: I think a parent as a whole would be fine, Sir. It doesn’t have to be a mother.
: I think for her it does. But you might be right. I don’t know.
: That’s sort of another reason I’m doing this.
: You mean...you’re looking to act like more of a father figure to her?
: That’s the idea.
: Well, I think it’s a great one, Sir.
: Though, it does further complicate the fact that she wants to harbor your offspring.
: Yeah. That’s a thing I’d really like her to stop wanting as soon as possible.
: Yeah. But that’s something I can deal with another day.
: There’s another reason I called, you know.
: Aye...And I think I know what it might be if it has anything to do with where this conversation’s currently headed.
: You were essentially just raised by your dad, right?
: Aye, Sir.
: Then, do you have any tips for me? Things that maybe he did that I can...try and probably fail at?
: Tips, you say?
: Yeah. Anything that may have stuck out to you or...anything you appreciate all these years later.
: It’s not “all these years later, Sir.” My father is still helping me to this day. How do you think I can afford so many expensive figures and games with my part time cafe salary?
: So the key to parenting is to increase her allowance?
: It’s to be mindful of her wants and needs...and to always keep her in your heart and mind.
: But an increase in her allowance would work wonders as well, I’m sure.
: Got it. Thanks for your help, Molly.
: There’s no need to thank me, Sir. I’m just glad you called.
: I miss you.
: I know...
: And I’m sorry. For just...kind of vanishing the way I did. But things aren’t exactly easy right now and I just need some time to-
: You don’t owe me an apology, Sir.
: I know I don’t owe you one, but I want to give you one. And I also want you to know that it’s not just you I’ve been avoiding. It’s everyone.
: I know, Sir. I can hear the halls, remember?
: Right...yeah.
: Listen, I-
: How long will you be camping for, Sir?
: Just today I think.
: May I see you when you return?
: Maybe not right away, but...
: Soon.
: I’ll be looking forward to it.
: Why?
: Why do you think?
: Anyway! I must rail the Kendo Princess now. But I thank you again for the transmission, Sir.
: And feel free to reach out again should you need me for anything.
: Sounds good.
: Thanks, Molly.
I hang up the phone and slip it back into my pocket, wandering off once more in a direction I don’t know.
But that’s really what all of this is when you think about it.
Today is just one man’s journey through uncharted territory.
But it’s nice knowing there will always be an entire class full of girls to lend me an ear when I really need one.
Or, in Molly’s case-
someone who will lend me everything
Molly’s affection has increased to [molly_love]!
Now what should I do?
